lines.zh: 榜单上的分数年年创新高，实际用起来却还是会出错。
lines.en: Scores climb every year, yet real use still goes wrong.

lines.zh: 这不是模型突然变笨，而是分数和能力之间有一道缝。
lines.en: The model did not get dumber. A gap sits between score and ability.

lines.zh: 这一章要回答：我们到底怎么知道一个模型行不行。
lines.en: This chapter asks how we can actually tell whether a model works.

lines.zh: 先说结论：分数是能力的代理指标，不是能力本身。
lines.en: First, the claim: a score is a proxy, not ability itself.

lines.zh: 记住这句话，后面每一节都在给它加注脚。
lines.en: Hold that line. Every section after this adds a footnote to it.

lines.zh: 我们可以精确测量损失，但损失低不等于好用。
lines.en: We can measure loss precisely, but low loss is not usefulness.

lines.zh: 损失衡量的是对下一个词的预测有多准。
lines.en: Loss measures how well the next word is predicted.

lines.zh: 而人关心的是，它能不能帮我把问题解决掉。
lines.en: What people care about is whether it solves the problem.

lines.zh: 损失降低零点一，普通用户能感知到差别吗。
lines.en: Loss drops by 0.1. Does any user feel the difference?

lines.zh: MMLU 提高两分，意味着它更会写代码吗。
lines.en: MMLU rises two points. Does it write better code?

lines.zh: 聊天机器人在榜单上很强，用起来为什么还是笨。
lines.en: It tops the charts. So why is it still dumb in practice?

lines.zh: 基准的演化史，就是一场出题人和模型的军备竞赛。
lines.en: Benchmark history is an arms race between test writers and models.

lines.zh: 二零一八年 GLUE 考句子级理解，一共九个任务。
lines.en: In 2018 GLUE tested sentence-level understanding with nine tasks.

lines.zh: 二零二一年 MMLU 用五十七个学科、约一点四万道选择题考世界知识。
lines.en: In 2021 MMLU used 57 subjects and about 14,000 multiple-choice questions.

lines.zh: 同年 GSM8K 考小学应用题，约八千五百道。
lines.en: That year GSM8K added grade-school word problems, about 8,500.

lines.zh: HumanEval 只有一百六十四道手写 Python 函数题。
lines.en: HumanEval had only 164 hand-written Python function tasks.

lines.zh: 二零二五年 HLE 两千五百题，专家出，号称搜索不到。
lines.en: In 2025 HLE arrived: 2,500 expert questions said to be unsearchable.

lines.zh: 发布时前沿模型的准确率，只有个位数。
lines.en: Frontier models scored in the single digits at release.

lines.zh: 越难越窄：新基准只测旧基准刷不动的那一个尖。
lines.en: Harder means narrower: each new test targets the one remaining peak.

lines.zh: 评测方法大致分三派，每一派都有自己的偏差。
lines.en: Evaluation comes in three schools, each with its own bias.

lines.zh: 第一派是静态基准，选择题，判分完全自动。
lines.en: The first is static benchmarks: multiple choice, fully automatic.

lines.zh: 它便宜、可复现，但可以猜，也可能被污染。
lines.en: Cheap and reproducible, but guessable and open to contamination.

lines.zh: 第二派是人类盲评，Chatbot Arena 让用户匿名二选一。
lines.en: The second is human blind rating: Arena shows two anonymous answers.

lines.zh: 它最接近真实偏好，但它测的是喜欢，不是正确。
lines.en: Closest to real preference, but it measures liking, not truth.

lines.zh: 第三派是 LLM-as-judge，用更强的模型来打分。
lines.en: The third is LLM-as-judge: a stronger model hands out the score.

lines.zh: 它便宜、可扩展，和人类判断的相关性还不错。
lines.en: Cheap, scalable, and decently correlated with human judgment.

lines.zh: 让模型当裁判，先要承认它自己有偏好。
lines.en: Let a model judge, and admit it has preferences of its own.

lines.zh: 它偏爱排在前面的答案，这叫位置偏好。
lines.en: It favours the answer placed first: position bias.

lines.zh: 它也偏爱更长的回答，哪怕信息并没有更多。
lines.en: It favours longer answers, even when they carry no more information.

lines.zh: 它还偏爱同家族模型的输出，和排版漂亮的答案。
lines.en: It favours its own family, and answers that look well formatted.

lines.zh: 解决办法不是换裁判，而是照搬人类的制度设计。
lines.en: The fix is not a better judge but human-style institutions.

lines.zh: 随机交换顺序、隐藏身份、多裁判投票，再用人类标注校准。
lines.en: Randomize order, hide identity, poll judges, recalibrate on humans.

lines.zh: 比偏差更硬的问题，是数据污染，也就是考试泄题。
lines.en: Harder than bias is contamination: the exam paper leaked.

lines.zh: 测试题和答案就在语料里，它不是会做，而是记得。
lines.en: Test items and answers sit in the corpus. It remembers, it does not solve.

lines.zh: 第一种检测是 n-gram 重叠，看题目和语料有没有重合。
lines.en: First check: n-gram overlap between test items and corpus.

lines.zh: 第二种是 canary 字符串，在测试集里埋一个独特标记。
lines.en: Second: a canary string, a unique marker planted in the test set.

lines.zh: 然后看模型会不会把这个标记原样复述出来。
lines.en: Then see whether the model repeats that marker verbatim.

lines.zh: 第三种是扰动测试：改数字、换名字，再问一遍。
lines.en: Third: perturbation. Change numbers, swap names, ask again.

lines.zh: 三种办法都只是间接检查，没人能保证题库干净。
lines.en: All three are indirect checks. Nobody can certify a test set is clean.

lines.zh: 真会做的模型仍然答对，靠记得的模型立刻露馅。
lines.en: A model that can solve it still answers; one that memorized fails.

lines.zh: 心理测量学留下三把尺子，看榜单时都用得上。
lines.en: Psychometrics leaves three rulers, all useful on a leaderboard.

lines.zh: 第一把是信度：同一个模型多测几次，分数稳不稳。
lines.en: Reliability: test the same model again. Does the score hold?

lines.zh: 第二把是效度：这个测试有没有测到它声称的能力。
lines.en: Validity: does the test measure the ability it claims to measure?

lines.zh: 最关键的是构念效度：你说是推理，它考的是记忆。
lines.en: Construct validity is the crux: you claim reasoning, it tests recall.

lines.zh: 第三把是生态效度：实验室任务能不能代表真实使用。
lines.en: Ecological validity: does a lab task represent real use?

lines.zh: 所以看到高分，先问它到底测的是哪一种能力。
lines.en: So when you see a high score, first ask which ability it measured.

lines.zh: 这一问比分数本身有用得多，也更难回答。
lines.en: That question is worth more than the score, and harder to answer.

lines.zh: 幻觉是模型生成看似合理，实则错误的内容。
lines.en: A hallucination looks plausible and is wrong or unsupported.

lines.zh: 第一类是事实性幻觉：它把世界上的事情说错了。
lines.en: Factuality errors get the world wrong.

lines.zh: 比如爱因斯坦 1955 年出生，年份完全错位。
lines.en: Einstein was born in 1955? The year is simply off.

lines.zh: 第二类是忠实性幻觉：它偏离了你给的输入。
lines.en: Faithfulness errors drift away from the input you gave.

lines.zh: 让你总结一篇文章，它加进文章里没有的内容。
lines.en: Asked to summarize, it adds material the article never contained.

lines.zh: 还有一类是自洽性：同一个问题，两次回答互相矛盾。
lines.en: A third kind: two answers to one question contradict each other.

lines.zh: 共同点是，它擅长编故事，却从不标记这是我编的。
lines.en: The common thread: it tells stories and never flags them as invented.

lines.zh: 幻觉不是偶然的故障，而是训练方式的结构性副产品。
lines.en: Hallucination is not a random fault. It is structural to training.

lines.zh: 第一，目标不匹配：训练只奖励预测下一个词。
lines.en: First, the objective is mismatched: training rewards the next word.

lines.zh: 语料里像答案的文本更常见，于是它学会了自信补全。
lines.en: Answer-shaped text beats I don't know, so it completes confidently.

lines.zh: 第二，训练数据本身就有错误和过时的信息。
lines.en: Second, the training data itself holds errors and stale facts.

lines.zh: 第三，采样会选到低概率的词，偶尔就编了。
lines.en: Third, sampling sometimes picks a low-probability token and invents.

lines.zh: 第四，人类评分者偏爱有问必答，模型就少说不知道。
lines.en: Fourth, raters prefer an answer to no answer, so it stops saying so.

lines.zh: 它也没有知识边界的显式表示，不知道自己不知道。
lines.en: It also has no explicit representation of where its knowledge ends.

lines.zh: 校准问的是：它说九成把握，实际就对九成吗。
lines.en: Calibration asks: when it says ninety percent, is it right that often?

lines.zh: 完美校准的模型，置信度和准确率画出来是一条对角线。
lines.en: A calibrated model plots confidence against accuracy on the diagonal.

lines.zh: 实际模型常常过度自信：说九成五，只对七成。
lines.en: Real models are overconfident: ninety-five claimed, seventy delivered.

lines.zh: ECE 把预测按置信度分桶，桶里比较两个数。
lines.en: ECE buckets predictions by confidence and compares two numbers.

lines.zh: 一个是平均置信度，一个是实际准确率，差距取绝对值。
lines.en: Mean confidence versus accuracy, difference in absolute value.

lines.zh: 再按每个桶的样本量加权平均，就得到 ECE。
lines.en: Weight each bucket by its share of samples and average: that is ECE.

lines.zh: 气象预报早就回答过：关键不是多自信，而是自信可信。
lines.en: Weather forecasting learned it: value is not confidence, but trust.

lines.zh: 这就是 Goodhart 定律的评测版。
lines.en: This is the evaluation edition of Goodhart's law.

lines.zh: 当一个指标成为目标，它就不再是好指标。
lines.en: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.

lines.zh: 教育测量早就演过一遍：考试成了目标，教学变成刷题。
lines.en: Education ran it: make exams the goal and teaching becomes drilling.

lines.zh: 基准也一样：刷分成了目标，分数就不再代表能力。
lines.en: Benchmarks too: once score-chasing is the goal, scores stop meaning ability.

lines.zh: 于是模型学会的是考试技巧，而不是真本事。
lines.en: So the model learns exam tricks instead of real skill.

lines.zh: 这不是谁作弊，而是指标一旦可优化，就会被优化。
lines.en: Nobody cheats. A metric that can be optimized will be optimized.

lines.zh: 所以看到超越人类这种标题，先别急着转发。
lines.en: So when a headline says it beats humans, do not share it yet.

lines.zh: 第一问：这个基准测的到底是什么能力。
lines.en: Question one: what ability does this benchmark actually test?

lines.zh: 第二问：题库有没有污染，答案很可能是有的。
lines.en: Question two: is the test set contaminated? Very likely yes.

lines.zh: 第三问：人类基线是多少，又是谁测出来的。
lines.en: Question three: what is the human baseline, and who measured it?

lines.zh: MMLU 的人类专家约百分之八十九点八，那是一批特定标注者的成绩。
lines.en: MMLU human experts sit near 89.8 percent, a specific group of annotators.

lines.zh: 第四问：分数提高，对应真实场景的什么改善。
lines.en: Question four: what real-world improvement does the higher score imply?

lines.zh: 问完这四个问题，标题通常就缩水一半。
lines.en: Ask those four, and most headlines shrink by half.

lines.zh: 这一章的主线只有一句：分数是代理，不是能力。
lines.en: One line holds it together: a score is a proxy, not ability.

lines.zh: 基准在军备竞赛，污染让分数贬值，幻觉是副产品。
lines.en: Arms races, contamination, and hallucination as a by-product.

lines.zh: 校准和构念效度，是看榜单时要戴的两副眼镜。
lines.en: Calibration and construct validity are the lenses for leaderboards.

lines.zh: 前面十二章，我们一直在外面看模型的行为。
lines.en: For twelve chapters we have watched the model from the outside.

lines.zh: 下一章把模型打开，看它内部到底在算什么。
lines.en: Next we open it up and watch what it computes inside.

lines.zh: 那就是机制可解释性，全课最像神经科学的一章。
lines.en: That is mechanistic interpretability, the neuroscience-like chapter.
